footer: Each change is to a security control: approve it through your security approval (e.g. the ISSO) before it is listed in fapolicyd_approved. A host where fapolicyd was running and is not after the change - or a program no longer starts - gets every file put back.

sections.text: Each line is a change (its hosts, why and what it does: below). Getting fapolicyd running first - its trust files, labels, db_max_size, enabled at boot, started permissive - then trust entries for what it blocked, container rules, the rules files' clean-up, and back to enforcing on a quiet day. To make them: the workflow's approval step, or by hand - list them in fapolicyd_approved exactly as here and run the job again (a Check run first). A db_max_size line may end in your own number.
